title: Common envelope
description: The provenance every record carries. Kind schemas in v1/ reference these property definitions one by one, because the validator's keyword subset has no allOf.

id.description: Slug; immutable once merged; equals the file name.

aliases.description: Former ids only. Unique across all ids and all other aliases.

authors.description: Contributors to this record, set from the issue opener by the Action. Never free text alone.

license.description: Validated per directory (rule 12). CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 exists for imported geometry, which data/LICENSE does not cover; it is allowed under data/presences/ and, for the actors an import creates, under data/actors/.

origin.description: Which writer created this record. Written once, by whatever created it, and never by an enrichment pass that fills in a field on somebody else's record: `origin` answers "who wrote this record", not "who has touched it" (rule 29). Absent means a person wrote it by hand. This is what the licence exception, the review queue and the imports key on, instead of matching an author's name against a literal string (health review A, findings 22 and 24; review B, finding 31).

tool.description: The writer. `cshapes` and `wikidata` are the two imports, `assistant` is the drafting exception in CLAUDE.md, `form` is the contribution pipeline. Closed, for the reason the edge types are: a writer nobody has decided about is a line added here.

run.description: Which run of that tool, where the tool has a name for one: a branch, a date, an input digest. Optional, and never load-bearing.

retraction.description: Why this record was retracted, and when. Present exactly on a retracted record (rule 27). It is the record's own history and nothing deletes it — signing a tombstone clears what the reviewer was asked to look at and leaves this alone, which is what `review.note` could not promise (health review B, finding 16).

reason.description: Written by a person, like an explanation: the argument for withdrawing the record, not a label.

review.description: What a reviewer should look at before signing this record, and why, and whether anybody has. Optional, and written by whoever drafted it. `status` and `signedBy` are the record's standing; `flags` and `citations` are the reviewer's to clear. Never a claim about the world — only about how much the record has been checked.

status.description: `draft` is a record no person has read; `reviewed` is one somebody has read and signed, and requires `signedBy` (rule 28). Absent means neither has been claimed. This is what "unreviewed" means, in place of an author's name matching a literal string (health review A, finding 8).

signedBy.description: Who signed this record and on what day. An array because a record can be read by more than one person; the reviewer is also added to `authors`, which is attribution — this is the act.

citations.description: Which of this record's citations a person has opened and checked against the source itself, keyed by the cited source's id (rule 3 checks the key is a source the record cites). A citation with no entry here has not been checked; the validator counts those and Sign warns about them without blocking. Never a claim about the world — only about how far this record has been read.

verified.description: Who checked this citation and on what day; null is a citation somebody looked at and did not confirm, which is not the same as one nobody has opened.

wikidata.description: The Wikidata item this record is about: Q followed by digits. Optional and additive — written by the import, or derived by the contribution form from a pasted Wikidata URL — and unique among records of the same kind (rule 21). It is an identifier and never a source: what the atlas asserts is in the record.

wikipedia.description: Language code to article title: { "en": "Carnation Revolution" }. Allowed only beside a wikidata id (rule 21), because a title with no item behind it is a guess about which article is meant. Written by the import.

body.description: The full entry: an extensive text about this event, actor or place, written by a person in the safe Markdown subset src/markdown.js renders (paragraphs, ## and ### headings, emphasis, lists, block quotes, links to records by id and to http(s) URLs, and citation marks [^source-id] that must resolve to this record's own sources — rule 23). No raw HTML and no images. Optional: the summary is what the cards show and this is the long form, so a record without one carries no key at all.

sitelinks.description: How many language editions have an article for the item, and the day that number was read. A count of somebody else's database changes without this record changing, so it is stored as a snapshot with its date rather than as a fact (health review A, finding 23b). A stored fact for an editorial decision nobody has taken: it feeds neither prominence nor weight, and the map's measure stays the derived weight (ARCHITECTURE.md).

sources.description: Citations. A citation points at a source record by id, with an optional locator (page, chapter, folio).
